governing_thought: Economics is divided by who settles an allocation: individuals and households, firms and markets, governments and public institutions, and the economy as a whole.
rank_note: Ranked from the smallest settling agent, the individual, to the largest, the whole economy.

pillars.title: Individuals and households
pillars.statement: Individuals and households settle allocations through their own choices about consumption, work, learning, health and risk.

pillars.title: Firms and markets
pillars.statement: Firms and markets settle allocations through production, exchange, pricing and competition in labour, product, financial, land and resource markets.

pillars.title: Governments and public institutions
pillars.statement: Governments and public institutions settle allocations through law, regulation, taxation, public choice and the redistribution of welfare.

pillars.title: The whole economy
pillars.statement: The whole economy settles allocations in aggregate through money, prices, growth, development and trade between countries.

method_line.title: Method line
method_line.covers: the history of economic thought, methodology, econometrics, teaching and reference material
